qa.q: What do you often do in the evening?
qa.a: Uh, it's a pretty set routine to be honest. Uh, on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday, I'll go to the gym after school and then head home. Uh, have dinner and go to bed. And Tuesday and Friday are a bit more open, and sometimes I go out or have people around, but more often I'll do work like writing. So, well, either way, it's not terribly riveting, sadly.

qa.q: Do you prefer to spend your evening with family or friends?
qa.a: I actually prefer to spend it by myself. I spend the whole day around people, but if I have to spend it with people, I don't mind which group, to be honest. I suppose my friends are more accessible at the moment, so I'd spend it with them. But that's more by virtue of proximity than preference.

qa.q: Do you ever work or study in the evenings?
qa.a: I try not to these days, but, um, it happens sometimes when there's a lot to do. So usually I'll set aside an hour or so for it and no more, but it has a habit of escalating still sometimes.

qa.q: What's a popular activity for people in your country in the evenings?
qa.a: I'm not sure. Um, everything is a bit radically different these days. I say a bit radically different. It is radically different. Uh, due to the crisis. Uh, though I imagine some people still eat together in the evenings, watch the local news, and have some kind of fun like playing games or going out.

qa.q: Do you do the same thing in the evenings as you did when you were a child?
qa.a: No, not quite. There's a lot less homework and walking for starters. Uh, I think there's more alone time too, so solo activities are more of a thing.
